Exercised each path with utm_data {utm_medium:'cpc',utm_term:'jsonb_probe'} and a fresh email, then in test_frr (bash -lic 'cd /Users/jessica/wrk/wrk-corp/inflow-ats && test_frr /tmp/utm_jsonb_probe.rb') reloaded and printed class/inspect/keys/equality + raw SQL. RESULT: ALL THREE PATHS CLEAN string-keyed Hashes; NO stringified ActionController::Parameters, NO {"parameters":...,"permitted":...} wrapper, NO symbol keys, absent input => nil (never {}).

PATH A (#create, HTTP POST /api/v1/sign_up, no name key) user id=39393: utm_data.class=Hash; inspect={"utm_term"=>"jsonb_probe", "utm_medium"=>"cpc"}; keys.map(&:class).uniq=[String]; ==expected true; raw SQL User.connection.select_value = "{\"utm_term\": \"jsonb_probe\", \"utm_medium\": \"cpc\"}" (proper JSON object). [expanded_params = sign_up_params.merge(...) is a PERMITTED ActionController::Parameters; User.new -> assign_attributes -> sanitize_for_mass_assignment.to_h converts nested utm_data to a plain Hash before assignment -> clean.]

PATH B (#magic_create, HTTP POST /api/v1/magic_login, login_intent:'hire' to route around M2 connect nil-crash) user id=39394: utm_data.class=Hash; inspect={"utm_term"=>"jsonb_probe", "utm_medium"=>"cpc"}; keys.map(&:class).uniq=[String]; ==expected true; raw SQL = "{\"utm_term\": \"jsonb_probe\", \"utm_medium\": \"cpc\"}". THIS IS THE HIGH-RISK PATH: user_params is a plain Ruby Hash whose :utm_data value is the nested PERMITTED ActionController::Parameters (sign_up_params[:utm_data]); it is NOT to_h'd because the plain hash doesn't respond to permitted?, so the raw Parameters object is passed straight to utm_data=. Empirically ActiveSupport::JSON.encode of that permitted Parameters serialized to a CLEAN JSON object in the DB (byte-identical to Path A) -- no wrapper corruption.
